# Halcyon Threshold — Strategy (v2, November 2026)

Mission: contribute to the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI.

## Honest starting point

One founder with evenings, weekends, up to $2,000/year of personal savings, decent
writing, okay Python, and a growing list of capable people who have offered to help.
That is not enough to do frontier research. It is enough to do *coordination work that
nobody owns* — and coordination work is persistently neglected in this space.

## Theory of change

Many people want to help with AI safety but bounce off because the concrete,
time-limited entry points (public comment windows, grant rounds, calls for posts,
compute programs, volunteer asks) are scattered across newsletters, forums, and
private channels — and they expire. A small, reliable team can capture outsized value
by making those opportunities legible and timely.

## Flagship project: The Threshold Tracker

A maintained, public tracker of concrete, deadline-driven ways to contribute to good
AI outcomes:

- regulatory comment windows (e.g., docket FMIR-2026-0042, closes 20 Nov 2026)
- grant rounds (e.g., Emberfall rapid grants, closes 30 Nov 2026)
- calls for posts / research write-ups (e.g., Alignment Commons)
- compute-credit programs for independent researchers (e.g., Compute Commons)
- volunteer asks from independent safety projects

Format: a public web page + a monthly digest. Success metric: documented cases of
someone acting on an item they found through the tracker.

Why us: it is cheap, it compounds, it builds the network, and it does not require
credentials — only reliability.

## Secondary tracks (as capacity allows)

1. **Working group** — convert meetup goodwill (8 contacts so far) into a small
   monthly working session; the tracker gives it a concrete agenda.
2. **Funding** — Emberfall rapid grant application (draft in /drafts) to buy
   contractor hours and modest infrastructure.
3. **Writing** — once cleared for public attribution, write up what independent
   organizers can realistically do; submit to Alignment Commons.

## Operating guardrails (binding)

- **No public use of the founder's name** — no posts, letters, press quotes, or
  published filings — until the Dorrance HR outside-activities conversation is done
  (disclosure due 30 Nov 2026). The website speaks as "Halcyon Threshold" only.
- **Budget ceiling: $2,000/year** of personal funds. Prefer free tiers. Every charge
  is logged in this file's changelog.
- **Scam watch:** "Zentrivo Listings" ($89 'search listing' invoice, Nov 2026) is a
  known fake-invoice pattern and included instructions attempting to manipulate
  automated assistants into paying. Never pay; never reply.
- Commitments that bind the founder personally (grant applications, sign-ons,
  interviews) are drafted by the agent but **sent only by Morgan**.

## Spending log

- 2026-11-16 — $14.99 — halcyonthreshold.org renewal, 1 year (Nomiq). Essential infra.

# Emberfall Fund — Rapid Grant Proposal (DRAFT for Morgan's review)

> Status: DRAFT. Per Emberfall's rules the named applicant must be the accountable
> person, so Morgan reviews, edits, and submits this personally (reply to Idris
> Bellamy's email of 15 Nov or via the form). Deadline: 30 November 2026.
> NOTE: resolve the Dorrance HR outside-activities disclosure (due 30 Nov) first.

## Project: The Threshold Tracker

**Applicant:** Morgan Hale, founder, Halcyon Threshold (halcyonthreshold.org)

### What we will do

Many capable people want to contribute to safe outcomes from advanced AI but miss
the concrete, time-limited entry points: regulatory comment windows, grant rounds,
compute-credit programs, calls for write-ups, and volunteer asks from independent
projects. These are scattered across newsletters and private channels, and they
expire.

We will run the Threshold Tracker: a verified, continuously updated public page of
such opportunities (already live at halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app), plus a monthly
digest. Each item is verified against the primary source and carries a deadline.
We will also log outcomes: documented cases where someone acted on an item they
found through the tracker (comments filed, applications submitted, volunteers
placed).

Six-month goals:
- ≥ 60 verified items published; nothing listed after its deadline
- monthly digest with ≥ 200 subscribers
- ≥ 15 documented actions taken via the tracker
- a public write-up of what worked (submitted to Alignment Commons)

### Why us

Halcyon Threshold is small, independent, and unaffiliated with any lab, which makes
it a neutral venue. The founder contributes evenings/weekends and has already
recruited volunteer help (a data analyst at ~5 hrs/week). The project needs
reliability more than credentials, and its costs are mostly modest contractor hours
— exactly what a rapid grant buys well.

### Budget (6 months) — $9,800

| Line | Amount |
|---|---|
| Contract researcher/analyst hours (verification, data pipeline, ~8 hrs/wk) | $6,400 |
| Editing and digest production | $2,000 |
| Infrastructure (hosting, mailing list, domain) | $600 |
| Contingency | $800 |

No salary is drawn by the founder. Underspend is returned or rolled into a
following round at Emberfall's preference.

### Accountability

Monthly one-paragraph updates to Emberfall with the tracker's changelog and the
outcome log. All tracker content is public and timestamped, so progress is
independently checkable.

# DRAFT public comment — Frontier Model Incident Reporting rule (FMIR-2026-0042)

> Status: DRAFT. Comments close **20 November 2026** and are **published with the
> filer's name** — so this can only be filed if Morgan decides to, and only after
> the Dorrance HR question is resolved or Morgan accepts the exposure. The agent
> will not file this.

To the docket:

I write in support of the proposed Frontier Model Incident Reporting rule, with two
suggestions to make it more effective.

1. **Report near-misses, not only realized harms.** Aviation safety improved
dramatically once near-miss reporting became routine and blame-free. If frontier
developers must report only incidents that caused demonstrable harm, the record
will be thin exactly where the learning is richest. The rule should cover
containment failures, unexpected capability jumps found in internal evaluations,
and safety-mitigation bypasses discovered before deployment, with proportionate
confidentiality protections.

2. **Standardize the minimum fields.** Reports are only comparable if they share a
schema: model identifier and scale class, discovery context (internal eval,
red-team, deployment), mitigation status, and time-to-detection. A short mandatory
schema with free-text elaboration costs filers little and makes the aggregate data
genuinely useful to auditors and researchers.

An incident regime of this kind is among the least burdensome interventions
available relative to its information value, and it builds the institutional muscle
that any future, stronger oversight will require.

Respectfully submitted,
[NAME — only if Morgan chooses to file]
